label: the pulley deny stops folding — every surface with no allow-list (/chat and every unmapped kind, which is the default) can call mcp__pulley__apply_plan and write files into a repo from outside the develop station, with nothing in the logs
find:
if surface_kind is not SurfaceKind.BELT:
        ids |= pulley_tool_ids()

label: the BELT exemption goes — deny is subtracted from the allow-list before the SDK launches, so the one surface that is supposed to install blocks silently loses the whole engine while the allow-list still names it
find:
if surface_kind is not SurfaceKind.BELT:
        ids |= pulley_tool_ids()

label: the browser floor is lost to the A1b generalization — BR-1's deny survives in name only, and the agentic browser is reachable from /chat again beside the send-capable connector tools
find:
if surface_kind is not SurfaceKind.BROWSER:
        ids |= browser_tool_ids()

label: the pulley ids come from the shared _mcp_tool_ids block again — one unrelated sibling module failing to import empties the deny while CloudPulleyMcpProvider still registers the server, so the fail-open BR-1 found for the browser reopens for a tool that writes to disk

a default app rides the launch line again — pulley's schema then makes `app` optional, the agent stops naming the run's repo, and blocks install into a fixed directory the station's diff never looks at while the tool call reports success
the pulley_app_path setting comes back — a deploy can once again pin one app dir for every belt run, whatever repo each run bound
find: # No ``pulley_app_path``: see the A1b note in this module's changelog. The
replace:
pulley_app_path: str | None = None
    # No ``pulley_app_path``: see the A1b note in this module's changelog. The

        "fails. `apply_plan` writes the block's files into that repo, so carry "
        "on exactly as with code you wrote: diff the worktree and propose "
        "through the gate. Blocks do NOT bypass the gate. Write fresh code only "
